subject: seahorse
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact upright seahorse model, roughly 15cm tall, facing forward, with the curled tail's lowest point touching the ground plane to satisfy the floor-contact rule.

Working out the spine geometry, I'm sketching an S-curve of coordinate points running from the head down through the neck, chest, belly, and hip, then into a spiraling tail that curls forward and down to meet the ground near y=0.

I'm planning the chain structure: one continuous catmull path from head to tail swept into joints, likely split into separate neck, spine, and tail chains for better control, all parented to a root joint positioned near the belly.

I'm defining the head pitch and neck taper with elliptical cross-sections getting thinner toward the top, plus a tail sweep tapering from the belly down through the hip and curling to a fine point with low-poly circular sections.

For the head, I'm setting up a skull sphere with a separate upper snout rod tilting down-forward and a hinged lower jaw rod beneath it, positioning both near the neck tip.

Adding eyes as small spheres with pupils on either side of the head, plus a crown of spike cones on top. Now I'm working out the dorsal fin as a thin extruded membrane along the back, figuring out the orientation vectors so the outline sweeps correctly in the y-z plane.

I need to work out where the fin should attach along the body's back surface, tracing how body radius and z-offset vary from hip to neck so the fin base follows the body contour rather than floating. I'll start the fin near z=-0.003 and extend it backward to about -0.03.

Now I'm giving the fin a pale translucent orange color and adding subtle horizontal stripe texturing. For pectoral fins, I'm planning small flattened spheres positioned near the head, scaled thin in one axis to look like round side fins.

For the body, I'm choosing a warm orange-yellow base and layering mottled, wobbly dark-brown stripes running along the y-axis to give it a natural banded pattern, applying the same stripe treatment to the tail for consistency.

For spine spikes, I'm working out orientation issues with the sweep frames and deciding it's simpler to manually compute spine positions along the known polyline and place small cones pointing outward from the back.

Working out radius functions and path coordinates for the neck, belly, and tail chains, keeping the body laterally compressed with narrower side-width than depth, and plotting the tail's curling points and tapering radius down to its tip.

Catmull-Rom interpolation should smooth things out fine. For the floor, the lowest tail point sits near zero, so I'll sink it slightly to 0.0065, with the head crown height around 0.165; I'll skip ring segments on the tail ridge and use paint stripes instead, then move on to positioning the neck chain at the top of the head.

I'm laying out a curved neck path leading into a joint hierarchy -- the neck bends back then the head tilts forward, with a head joint parented to the last neck link pointing forward-down. The head itself is an oriented ellipsoid at a specific position, with a tapered snout rod extending forward and the jaw joint coming next.

Now I'm working out the jaw geometry -- positioning the lower jaw rod so its tapered radius aligns with the upper snout's underside, adjusting endpoints so the two surfaces meet without overlap or gaps, then placing the eyes as small spheres with contrasting pupils.

I'm also planning the coronet spikes as backward-tilted cones arranged around the top of the head, and the pectoral fins as scaled, flattened spheres positioned along the neck's taper, working out their placement coordinates relative to the neck radius.

Mirroring both fins symmetrically, I decide each should get a dedicated hinge joint attached to the neck chain rather than using the nearest default bone, naming them finL and finR. I'm also sketching in optional dorsal fin joints and small snout spot details, then setting up how spikes along the back will be evaluated along the neck's curve at specific parameter positions.

Positioning the tail spikes along a curved path, I'm defining their placement, direction, and cone dimensions, then moving to the paint logic -- using a stripe pattern over a mottled base color for the body sweeps while keeping the head and snout a plain solid tone, and wiring up the chain using a catmull spline for the neck path.

Finishing the sweep call with radius function, sides, and color, then exporting the final meta -- done.
